terms: (phase == D1) * choice ;; (phase == GO) * choice ;; (phase == D2) * (state == S2) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_reward == 1) ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_action == 2) ;; (phase == GO) * (last_is("a2 S1 u") - last_is("a1 S2 u")) ;; (phase == D2) * choice ;; (phase == D2) * (prev_reward == 1)
explanation: Reset gate r of unit 42. It is always on and rises steeply late in the episode; that timing is in the baseline, which explains R^2 0.44. Beyond timing, the unit is mainly an a2/S2-side signal. At D2 the biggest effect is reaching S2 (+0.09). At D1 and GO it rises as the policy logit leans toward a2 (choice is negative; this is a model quantity, not a future variable). At D1 it is higher after a rewarded previous trial (+0.06). At GO it is higher after a previous a2 choice (+0.03), and higher still after a2 S1 u, while it is lower after a1 S2 u (+-0.035). At D2 it is slightly lower after a rewarded previous trial. Value, this trial reward and trials since reversal add essentially nothing; the good-state effect (0.21 alone) is carried by choice and state. Multiplying the terms by an episode-time gain fit worse (0.54 dev). 8 terms: dev R^2 beyond timing 0.674, test 0.670 (all ceiling 0.80, all observed 0.75). Remaining errors: over-predicts after unrewarded a2 S2 trials at GO and D2, and under-predicts at the largest late-episode values.

(phase == GO) * (last_is("a2 S1 u") - last_is("a1 S2 u"))

issues: Reproduced the reported score: test R^2 beyond timing is 0.670 (dev 0.674). Every term contributes on test. Dropping D2*choice gives 0.650, dropping D2*prev_reward gives 0.657, dropping GO*prev_action gives 0.656. The fitted signs match the explanation: choice weights are negative, so the gate rises as the logit leans toward a2. D2*S2 is +0.091, D1*prev_reward is +0.059, GO*prev_action==2 is +0.033, GO*(a2S1u - a1S2u) is +0.035 and D2*prev_reward is -0.025.

The claims that 'value, this reward, since-reversal and good state add nothing' hold. Adding each as an 8th term to the 7 other terms gives 0.656 (value), 0.657 (this reward), 0.657 (since_rev) and 0.659 (good), against a 7-term base of about 0.65.
The claim that 'episode-time scaling fits worse' also holds. Multiplying every term by (1+ep_dec) gives 0.647 test, and multiplying by exp(ep_trial/25) gives 0.512.

Residual error class 1, already acknowledged: the model over-predicts after a2 S2 u at GO (-0.046) and D2 (-0.052). This is only partly fixed by extending the last-trial terms to GO and D2 and subtracting a2 S2 u: 0.688 test.

Residual error class 2, already acknowledged: the worst-fit windows are all trials 91-99 in a2/S2c streaks, under-predicted by roughly 0.15-0.25. A late-time x choice term (ep_trial^2*choice) helps only a little (about +0.01). The largest late-episode values stay unexplained.

The label leans on 'choice' (the model's policy logit, a model-output quantity) at D1 and GO. The variables help says choice is only meaningful at GO. An observed-only rewrite that replaces choice with prev_action / last-trial terms drops to 0.523, so the policy read-out carries real extra signal. The explanation correctly calls choice a model quantity.

There is still a gap to the ceilings: 0.67 against 0.75 (all observed) and 0.80 (all). With at most 8 terms I could not close it beyond about 0.70. The remaining errors are moderate (largest phase x previous-trial bias about 0.04 after my rewrite), not a large uncaptured systematic class.
